in_hebrew.name: פאוסטינה
in_hebrew.meaning: פאוסטינה: שם שמקורו בלטיני, פירוש: 'דבוקה' או 'קשורה'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פאוסטינה: שם שמקורו בלטיני, המיוחס לטריבון הרומי, פאוסטינוס. 'דבוקה' או 'קשורה' בעברית. במסורת הנוצרית, השם קשור לאגדה של סנטה פאולה, שכונתה 'Faustina' והייתה אחותה של אגנס, שהפכה לנזירה. פאוסטינה, כנצרכה, סייעה לאגנס לתמוך בכמה בעיות, ולבסוף, הפכה לאחותה של אגנס. שם זה נחשב, לעיתים, כאחד מ'שמות הדבקה', ובכך, נחשב כאחד השמות, שלא מייצגים 'פאוסט' בספרות קלאסית, כגון, 'Faust' (גבול) ו'Faustus' (בעל), אלא 'Faustina', שפירושו 'דבוקה' או 'קשורה'.

in_greek.name: Φαυστίνα
in_greek.meaning: Φαυστίνα: όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική, περιγραφή: 'αγκαλούνμενη' ή 'συνδεδεμένη'
in_greek.long_meaning: Φαυστίνα: όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική, που ανήκει στον Τριβούνο Ρωμαίο Φαυστίνο. 'Αγκαλούνμενη' ή 'συνδεδεμένη' στην ελληνική γλώσσα. Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα συνδέεται με τη μυθική ιστορία της Αγίας Φαουστίνας, που ήταν αδελφή της Αγίας Αγνής. Η Φαουστίνα, ως αρωγή, βοήθησε την Αγνή να αντιμετωπίσει αρκετές δυσκολίες, και τελικά, έγινε αδελφή της Αγνής. Το όνομα αυτό θεωρείται, από καιρού σε καιρό, ως ένα από τα 'όνοματα της συνδεσιμότητας', και ως such, θεωρείται ως ένα από τα ονόματα που δεν αναπαριστούν την 'Φαύστο' στην κλασική γραμματεία, όπως το 'Φαύστ' (άκρη) και το 'Φαύστος' (ανήρ), αλλά το 'Φαουστίνα', που σημαίνει 'αγκαλούνμενη' ή 'συνδεδεμένη'.

in_latin.name: Faustina
in_latin.meaning: Faustina: nomen originum a Latina, interpretatio: 'vinculum' vel 'connecta'
in_latin.long_meaning: Faustina: nomen originum a Latina, quod tribuno Romano Faustino pertinet. 'Vinculum' vel 'connecta' in lingua Latina. In traditione Christiana, nomen coniungitur ad fabulam de Sancta Faustina, sorore Sanctae Agnetis. Faustina, ut ancilla, auxilio Agneti contra multas difficultates, et tandem, Agnetis soror facta est. Nomen hoc putatur, ex tempore in tempus, esse unum ex 'nominibus connexionis', et ita, putatur esse unum ex nominibus, quae non manifestant 'Faustum' in litteris classicis, ut 'Faust' (fines) et 'Faustus' (vir), sed 'Faustina', quae significat 'vinculum' vel 'connecta'.

in_english.name: Faustina
in_english.meaning: Faustina: name of Latin origin, meaning: 'bonded' or 'connected'
in_english.long_meaning: Faustina: name of Latin origin, associated with the Roman Tribune Faustinus. 'Bonded' or 'connected' in English. In Christian tradition, the name is linked to the legendary story of Saint Faustina, who was the sister of Saint Agnes. Faustina, as a helpmate, assisted Agnes in overcoming many difficulties, and eventually, became Agnes' sister. This name is considered, from time to time, as one of the 'names of connection', and as such, is considered as one of the names that do not represent 'Faust' in classical literature, such as 'Faust' (borders) and 'Faustus' (man), but 'Faustina', which means 'bonded' or 'connected'.

saint_reference.note: Faustina Kowalska was a Polish nun and mystic. She is known for her visions and writings, which were later compiled into the 'Divine Mercy in My Soul' diary. She is revered as a saint in the Catholic Church and is known for her role in popularizing the devotion to the Divine Mercy.

data.cultural_impact: The name Faustina has a rich history in various Christian traditions. In the Roman Catholic Church, there is a popular devotion to Saint Faustina Kowalska, a Polish nun who is believed to have received visions and messages from Jesus, requesting the establishment of the Divine Mercy Doctrine. Her Diary, revealing these messages, was published after her death in 1937 and quickly gained popularity, leading to her canonization in 2005. Today, Saint Faustina is widely known as the Apostle of Mercy.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Faustina' holds significant spiritual importance as it is connected to the courageous figure of Saint Faustina Kowalska. Her deep spiritual experiences and unwavering faith in God's mercy have inspired and touched millions around the world. Her life story exemplifies how even the smallest among us can affect great change in the world through faith and obedience. Traditions such as the Divine Mercy Novena, held annually on Good Friday, and the image of the Divine Mercy, in which Jesus is depicted with his right hand raised in blessing and his left hand touching his Heart, are powerful reminders of the spiritual legacy Faustina leaves behind.
